thread:
anya: kicking off a concise rollup of the GPTQ bake I ran across Llama-2-13B, Mistral-7B-v0, and Qwen-7B. short TL;DR then a couple of gotchas below.

mike: thanks — excited to see numbers. did you keep the eval harness identical across families?

anya: yep — same harness, same eval-sets (MMLU subset, Lambada, TruthfulQA short, and a small instruction-safety probe). deterministic seeds, same prompt templates.

sofia: great. what quant configs did you try?

anya: primary sweep: GPTQ 4-bit (group size 128, per-channel scales), GPTQ 6-bit, and AWQ-8 with per-tensor fallback for attention qk. also ran a tiny FP8 baseline via XLA for comparison (not production-ready).

raj: curious about perf/mem tradeoffs — any numbers on peak device memory and latency?

anya: short table (approx):
```
Model          | FP32 mem | GPTQ-4 mem | AWQ-8 mem |  p50 tok/ms
Llama-2-13B    | 40GB     | 11GB       | 15GB      |  FP32 40, GPTQ-4 95, AWQ-8 68
Mistral-7B-v0  | 24GB     | 8.5GB      | 10GB      |  FP32 55, GPTQ-4 120, AWQ-8 82
Qwen-7B        | 28GB     | 9.2GB      | 11GB      |  FP32 48, GPTQ-4 102, AWQ-8 74
```
Numbers are on A100-40 (single-GPU), batch=1, seq=512.

oliver: wow GPTQ-4 gives big mem wins and latency improvements vs FP32. any quality regressions?

anya: yes — accuracy deltas vs FP32 (MMLU accuracy, Lambada perplexity) — headline: GPTQ-4 costs ~1.8-3.5% accuracy drop on MMLU depending on family; AWQ-8 is smaller at ~0.6-1.2% but larger mem than GPTQ-4. specifics:
```
Model     | MMLU delta (%) | Lambada ppx delta
Llama-13B | -3.5           | +9%
Mistral7B | -2.1           | +6%
Qwen7B    | -1.8           | +5%
```
Note: AWQ-8 deltas were roughly half these numbers except in one Mistral instruction subset where AWQ produced +2% hallucination rate on the safety probe.

eval-bot: automated eval summary attached: mmluscore_fp32=72.4; mmluscore_gptq4=69.1; mmluscore_awq8=71.6; lambada_ppx_fp32=12.1; lambada_ppx_gptq4=13.2; lambada_ppx_awq8=12.7.

mike: interesting. did you try smaller group sizes or per-layer tuning?

anya: yes — group size 32 improved Qwen a bit (MMLU -1.0% vs -1.8%), but increased memory by ~600MB and slowed quant/time by ~8%. Llama responded poorly to small groups (instability in a few heads).

sofia: any insights on KV cache or streaming differences?

anya: GPTQ artifacts caused slightly higher KV cache growth for Llama-13B in our runtime (looks like quantized linear math increased scratch allocation behavior). AWQ-8 had cleaner cache profile. For streaming low-latency use-cases AWQ-8 is a nicer drop-in.

raj: what about model-specific bits — e.g., Mistral's multihead layout or Qwen's layernorm placement — did that change results?

anya: yes — Mistral's fused attention kernels are sensitive to quantization noise in Q/K projections. We saw a consistent small bias in top-k logits that inflated certain instruction outputs (hence +2% hallucination on the safety probe). Qwen was the most robust overall — likely due to its layernorm ordering and wider activation distributions that compress better under per-channel scaling.

oliver: any deploy recommendations for each customer tier (hosted vs dedicated)?

anya: quick suggestions:
- Hosted (latency-sensitive): AWQ-8 as default for Mistral & Qwen; GPTQ-4 for Llama only if the customer tolerates the MMLU delta. Add an automatic fallback to AWQ on error/regression.
- Dedicated (cost-sensitive, predictable throughput): GPTQ-4 with canary rollout + per-model group-size tuning. Use block-size=128 except for Qwen where group=32 if you can accept mem hit.
- Private/on-prem: expose both quant variants and let ops pick via route policy. Provide eval bundles so customers can run the same MMLU/lambada probe locally.

sofia: ops question — does our serving runtime need kernel changes to better support GPTQ-4?

anya: yes — two quick asks: 1) reduce scratch realloc churn for quantized matmuls (we can reuse buffers across KV steps), 2) add a fast path for per-channel dequant in attention q/k to reduce top-k bias. Both should reduce GPTQ-4 latency by ~10-15% and mitigate some accuracy drift.

mike: next steps?

anya: proposed action items:
- run longer eval (10k MMLU samples) for the three winners (QA + reasoning subsets) — @raj to schedule on the sweep cluster
- re-run GPTQ-4 with group=32 for Qwen + group=128 for others and collect headwise logit deltas — @oliver
- add AWQ-8 canary to hosted default path for Qwen/Mistral and monitor hallucination/safety metrics for 48h — @sofia
- engineering task: scratch reuse RFC and perf patch for per-channel attention dequant — I'll draft the PR

raj: assigned the long-eval to job 5217, starts in 20m. ETA ~6h.

oliver: starting the group-size reruns now, will post delta heatmaps to the thread.

sofia: adding the canary rollout doc to the deploy queue.

anya: thanks all — summary will go into the model-onboarding checklist and I'll attach the eval artifacts to the model card. ping if you need raw logs or the quant params. :white_check_mark:
